createColCircle.description:
This function creates a collision circle. This is a shape that has a position and a radius and infinite height that you can use to detect a player's presence. Events will be triggered when a player enters or leaves it.

{{VisualizeColshape}}

createColPolygon.description:
* **Note:** For this function to work correctly, get/set your bound points in an anti-clockwise fashion.

* **Note:** Even though this is a 2D colshape, [isElementWithinColShape](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/isElementWithinColShape) returns false if an element is in the area but below 0 Z height.

This function creates a collision polygon. See [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon Wikipedia] for a definition of a polygon. The first set of X Y of this shape is not part of the colshape bounds, so can set anywhere in the game world, however for performance, place it as close to the centre of the polygon as you can. It should be noted this shape is *2D*. There should be at least 3 bound points set.

{{VisualizeColshape}}

createColSphere.description:
This function creates a collision sphere. This is a shape that has a position and a radius. See [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere Wikipedia] for a definition of a sphere.

{{VisualizeColshape}}

createColTube.description:
This function creates a collision tube. This is a shape that has a position and a 2D (X/Y) radius and a height. See [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylinder_(geometry) Cylinder] for a definition of a tube. A tube is similar to a colcircle, except that it has a limited height, this means you can limit the distance above the position defined by (fX, fY, fZ) that the collision is detected.

{{VisualizeColshape}}

By default, a colshape polygon is infinitely tall.}}

* **Note:** This function only handles the cursor state set by the [showCursor](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/showCursor) function, ignoring it if the console, chatbox, or menu is open.

* **Note:** If you use this function on the server-side, keep in mind that it only detects the [showCursor](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/showCursor) function executed on the server-side and does not detect the function executed on the client-side.

* **Note:** Regardless of the cursor state you set using this function, the cursor will always be visible while the menu, the chatbox input line or the console are active, or if another resource has called this function.

* **Note:**  Be aware of that if showCursor enbaled by a resource you can't disabled it from a different ressource showCursor(false) will not works, in order to make it works, disable it from the original resource that enabled it or use export

addEvent.description: This function allows you to register a custom [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event). Custom events function exactly like the built-in events. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event system) for more information on the event system.

addEventHandler.description:
This function will add an [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event) handler. An event handler is a function that will be called when the event it's attached to is triggered. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event system) for more information on how the event system works.

{{Important Note|See [Script security](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Script security) for how-to prevent cheaters from abusing [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event system) and [element data](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element data).}}

* **Note:** You shouldn't re-use the same name for your handler function as the event name - if multiple handler functions are used, as this can lead to confusion. On the same note, for multiple reasons, it isn't a good idea to export the same functions that you use locally as remote event handlers.

Event handlers are functions that are called when a particular event happens. Each event specifies a specific set of variables that are passed to the event handler and can be read by your function. The following global variables are available for use in handler functions:

**source*: the element that triggered the event

**this*: the element that the event handler is attached to

**sourceResource*: the resource that triggered the event.

**sourceResourceRoot*: the root element ([getResourceDynamicElementRoot|dynamic element root](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getResourceDynamicElementRoot|dynamic element root) on client) of the resource that triggered the event.

**client*: the client that triggered the event using [triggerServerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/triggerServerEvent). Not set if the event was not triggered from a client.

{{New_feature|3|1.0|

**eventName*: the name of the event which triggered the handler function.

}}

It is important to remember that events pass up and down the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element tree). An event triggered on the root element is triggered on every element in the tree. An event triggered on any other element is triggered on its ancestors (its parent element and its parent's parent etc) and its children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. You can use the ''propagate'' argument to specify if you wish your handler to receive events that have propagated up or down the tree.

The order in which event handlers are triggered is undefined, you should not rely on one event handler being executed before another.

Each function closure can only be added once to each event. On the second attempt to add the function closure to the same event a warning will be emitted to the debug console and the call to addEventHandler will fail.

* **Note:** See [Event_Source_Element|Event Source Element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_Source_Element|Event Source Element) for a descriptive visualization of the event system handling an event trigger.

cancelEvent.description:
This function is used to stop the automatic internal handling of events, for example this can be used to prevent an item being given to a player when they walk over a pickup, by canceling the [onPickupUse](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/onPickupUse) event.

[cancelEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/cancelEvent) does not have an effect on all events, see the individual event's pages for information on what happens when the event is canceled. [cancelEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/cancelEvent) does not stop further event handlers from being called, as the order of event handlers being called is undefined in many cases. Instead, you can see if the currently active event has been cancelled using [wasEventCancelled](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/wasEventCancelled).

The use of cancelEvent outside of an event handler has no effect.

If you implement your own custom events and want to handle them being cancelled, you should call [wasEventCancelled](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/wasEventCancelled) to check after your call to [triggerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/triggerEvent).

cancelLatentEvent.description: Stops a latent event from completing

getLatentEventHandles.description: Gets the currently queued latent events. The last one in the table is always the latest event queued. Each returned handle can be used with [getLatentEventStatus](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getLatentEventStatus) or [cancelLatentEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/cancelLatentEvent)

getLatentEventStatus.description: Gets the status of one queued latent event.

removeEventHandler.description: This functions removes a handler function from an [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event), so that the function is not called anymore when the event is triggered. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event system) for more information on how the event system works.

triggerEvent.description:
This function will trigger a named [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event) on a specific [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element) in the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element tree). See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/event system) for more information on how the event system works.

You can use the value returned from this function to determine if the event was cancelled by one of the event handlers. You should determine what your response (if any) to this should be based on the event's purpose. Generally, cancelling an event should prevent any further code being run that is dependent on whatever triggered that event. For example, if you have an ''onFlagCapture'' event, cancelling it would be expected to prevent the flag being able to be captured. Similarly, if you have ''onPlayerKill'' as an event you trigger, canceling it would either be expected to prevent the player being killed from dying or at least prevent the player from getting a score for it.

* **Note:** You should avoid triggering events on the [root element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/root element) unless you really need to. Doing this triggers the event on every element in the element tree, which is potentially very CPU intensive. Use as specific (i.e. low down the tree) element as you can.

* **Note:** See [Event_Source_Element|Event Source Element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_Source_Element|Event Source Element) for a descriptive visualization of the event system handling an event trigger.

wasEventCancelled.description:
This function checks if the last completed event was cancelled. This is mainly useful for custom events created by scripts.

Events can be cancelled using [cancelEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/cancelEvent), this indicates that the resource which triggered the event should do whatever it can to reverse any changes made by whatever caused the event. See [triggerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/triggerEvent) for a more detailed explanation of this.

createExplosion.description: Creates an explosion of a certain type at a specified point in the world. If creator is specified, the explosion will occur only in its dimension.

fileClose.description: Closes a file handle obtained by [fileCreate](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/fileCreate) or [fileOpen](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/fileOpen).

fileCopy.description:
This function copies a file.

{{Tip|If you do not want to share the content of the created file with other servers, prepend the file path with @ (See [filepath](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/filepath) for more information)}}

fileExists.description: This functions checks whether a specified file exists inside a resource.

fileFlush.description: Forces pending disk writes to be executed. [fileWrite](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/fileWrite) doesn't directly write to the hard disk but places the data in a temporary buffer; only when there is enough data in the buffer it is actually written to disk. Call this function if you need the data written right now without closing the file. This is useful for log files that might want to be read while the resource is still executing. [fileFlush](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/fileFlush) can be called after each log entry is written. Without this, the file may appear empty or outdated to the user.

fileGetPos.description: Returns the current read/write position in the given file.

fileGetSize.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the given file.

fileIsEOF.description:
Checks if the file position is at the end of the file.

* **Note:** Due to underlying C API restrictions this function may return false until an attempt to read further than the end of the file is made.

fileRead.description: Reads the specified number of bytes from the given file starting at its current read/write position, and returns them as a string.

fileRename.description:
Renames the specified file.

* **Note:** Also with this function you can move specified file to a new location, new folder or even to another resource's folder. But for this action executing resource must have 'ModifyOtherObjects' ACL right set to ''true''.

fileSetPos.description: Sets the current read/write position in the file.

fileWrite.description: Writes one or more strings to a given file, starting at the current read/write position. Advances the position over the number of bytes that were written.

addCommandHandler.description:
{{Important Note|Do *NOT* use the same name for your handler function as the command name, as this can lead to confusion if multiple handler functions are used. Use a name that describes your handler's purpose more specifically.}}

This function will attach a scripting function (handler) to a console command, so that whenever a player or administrator uses the command the function is called.

Multiple command handlers can be attached to a single command, and they will be called in the order that the handlers were attached. Equally, multiple commands can be handled by a single function, and the ''commandName'' parameter used to decide the course of action.

For users, a command is in the format:

''commandName'' ''argument1'' ''argument2''

This can be triggered from the player's console or directly from the chat box by prefixing the message with a forward slash (''/''). For server side handlers, the server admin is also able to trigger these directly from the server's console in the same way as they are triggered from a player's console.

* **Note:** You can't use "check", "list", "test" and "help" as a command name.

bindKey.description:
Binds a player's key to a handler function or command, which will be called when the key is pressed.

* **Note:** Using *escape* key or *F8* key will always return false. Use [onClientKey](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/onClientKey) event instead.

* **Note:** Handler function won't be triggered while focused in CEGUI editbox. You can use [guiSetInputMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/guiSetInputMode) or [onClientKey](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/onClientKey) in order to fix that.

executeCommandHandler.description:
This function will call all the attached functions of an existing console command, for a specified player.

* **Note:** You can only execute commands created with addCommandHandler. You cannot execute MTA harcoded commands due to security reasons.

* **Note:** Serverside commands can only be executed by the server. The same applies to the client side

getFunctionsBoundToKey.description: Gets the functions bound to a key. To bind a function to a key use the [bindKey](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/bindKey) function

getKeyBoundToFunction.description: getKeyBoundToFunction allows retrieval of the first key bound to a function.

isControlEnabled.description: Checks whether a GTA control is enabled or disabled for a certain player.

removeCommandHandler.description: This function removes a command handler, that is one that has been added using [addCommandHandler](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/addCommandHandler). This function can only remove command handlers that were added by the resource that it is called in.

toggleAllControls.description: Enables or disables the use of all GTA controls for a specified player.

toggleControl.description:
Enables or disables the use of a GTA control for a specific player.

* **Note:**  If you want to disable weapons fire, remember to also disable the control *action* in addition to the control *fire*.

unbindKey.description:
Removes an existing key bind from the specified player.

* **Note:** unbindKey will only work on binds that were added by the same resource

* **Note:** unbindKey on the server may return ''true'' on failure

* **Note:** If you call unbindKey twice, it will break other scripts: [https://github.com/multitheftauto/mtasa-blue/issues/497 Issue 497]

getMarkerColor.description: This function returns the color and transparency for a marker element.

getMarkerCount.description:
Returns the number of markers that currently exist in the world.

getMarkerIcon.description: This function returns the icon name for a marker.

getMarkerSize.description: This function returns a [float](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/float) containing the size of the specified marker.

getMarkerTarget.description: This function returns the position of the specified marker's target, the position it points to. This only works for checkpoint markers and ring markers. For checkpoints it returns the position the arrow is pointing to, for ring markers it returns the position the ring is facing. You can set this target with [setMarkerTarget](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setMarkerTarget).

getMarkerTargetArrowProperties.description: {{New feature/item|9.0161|1.6.0|22620|function returns the color, transparency and size for a checkpoint marker's target arrow.}}

getMarkerType.description: This function returns a marker's type.

setMarkerColor.description: This function sets the color of the specified marker by modifying the values for red, green, blue and alpha.

setMarkerIcon.description: This function allows changing the icon of a checkpoint marker.

setMarkerSize.description:
This function sets the size of the specified marker.

Setting negative value will "flip" the marker, do nothing or make it invisible:

* *cylinder* or *arrow*: upside down

* *ring*: inside out

* *checkpoint*: disappear

* *corona*: bigger

setMarkerTarget.description:
This function sets the 'target' for a marker. Only the ''checkpoint'' and ''ring'' marker types can have a target.

For ''checkpoint'' markers, the target is shown as an arrow aiming at the point specified. Only 5 arrows can be visible at the same time.

For ''ring'' markers, the target is shown by rotating the whole ring so that it faces the point specified.

This function is most useful for setting up markers for races, where each marker points to the next one's position.

(This is mostly used in races!)

setMarkerTargetArrowProperties.description: {{New feature/item|9.0161|1.6.0|22620|This function changes the color and size of the checkpoint marker's target arrow.}}

setMarkerType.description: This function changes a marker's type. The type controls how the marker is displayed in the game. It's important that you use marker types that users are used to from the single player game. For example, checkpoints are used in races, rings are used for aircraft races, arrows are used for entering buildings etc.

breakObject.description:
This function breaks a specific object. {{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22489|This function is now also available on the server side.}}

* **Note:** Only breakable objects can be broken.

getObjectScale.description: This function returns the visible size of an object.

moveObject.description: This function will smoothly move an object from its current position to a specified rotation and position.

respawnObject.description:
This function respawns a specific object.

{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22708|This function is now also available on the server side.}}

isObjectRespawnable.description: {{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22708|This function checks if the object has respawn enabled, which can be toggled using [toggleObjectRespawn](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/toggleObjectRespawn).}}

setObjectScale.description:
This function changes the visible size of an object.

* **Note:** setObjectScale *does not* affect the collision models for the object, as such is unsuitable for use for interaction with players, vehicles or other objects.

isObjectMoving.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20811|This function checks if an [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/object) is moving.}} {{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22430|This function is now also available on the server side.}}

isObjectBreakable.description:
{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|21765|Added also as a server-side function. Previously only available as a client-side function.}}

This function checks if an object / model ID is breakable.

setObjectBreakable.description:
{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|21765|Added also as a server-side function. Previously only available as a client-side function.}}

This function sets an object to be breakable/unbreakable.

stopObject.description: This will allow you to stop an object that is currently moving.

clearChatBox.description: {{New feature/item|3.0156|1.5.5|14165|This function clears the chatbox. It does not clear the console (F8)}}

outputChatBox.description:
* **Note:** Avoid outputting text to the chatbox that isn't actually chat, as this can be annoying for players. Output information and status messages to the HUD.

This outputs the specified text string to the chatbox. It can be specified as a message to certain player(s) or all players.

It can optionally allow you to embed color changes into the string by setting the colorCoded boolean to true. This allows:

<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">

outputChatBox ( "#FF0000Hello #00FF00World", root, 255, 255, 255, true )

</syntaxhighlight>

This will display as: *<span style='color:red;'>Hello</span> <span style='color:green'>World</span> *

outputConsole.description: This outputs the specified text string to the console window (accessed with F8 or ~ key). It can be specified as a message to certain player(s) or all players.

outputDebugString.description: This function outputs scripting debug messages, which can be read by enabling the debug textbox. The debug display level can then be set so that info or warning messages get filtered out.

showChat.description: This function is used to show or hide the player's chat.

pathIsFile.description: {{Added feature/item|1.6.1|1.6.0|22470|Checks if a specified path points to a file.}}

pathIsDirectory.description: {{Added feature/item|1.6.1|1.6.0|22470|Checks if a specified path points to a directory.}}

createPickup.description: This function creates a pickup element, which is placed in the GTA world and can be picked up to retrieve a health, armour or a weapon.

getPickupAmmo.description: This function retrieves the amount of ammo in a weapon pickup.

getPickupAmount.description: This function retrieves the amount of health or armor given from a pickup.

getPickupType.description: This function retrieves the type of a pickup, either a health, armour or weapon pickup.

setPickupType.description: This function allows changing the type of a pickup to a Weapon, Armour or Health pickup, and allows you to set the health points *or* the weapon and ammo that the pickup will give.

detonateSatchels.description: This function can be used to detonate a players satchels.

createRadarArea.description: This function can be used to create custom radar areas on the radar.

getRadarAreaColor.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current color of a [radararea|radar area](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/radararea|radar area).

getRadarAreaSize.description: This function is used for getting the X and Y size of an existing [radararea|radar area](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/radararea|radar area).

isInsideRadarArea.description: This function checks if a 2D position is inside a [radararea|radar area](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/radararea|radar area) or not.

isRadarAreaFlashing.description: This function allows detection of whether a radar area is flashing or not.

setRadarAreaColor.description: Sets the color of an existing radar area.

setRadarAreaFlashing.description: This function makes an existing radar area flash in transparency.

setRadarAreaSize.description: This function changes the size of an existing [radararea|radar area](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/radararea|radar area).

getResourceConfig.description:
{{server client function}}

This function is used to return the root node of a configuration file. Config files must be predefined in a resource's [Meta.xml|meta file](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Meta.xml|meta file).  An alternative way to load XML files is to use [xmlLoadFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlLoadFile).

getResourceExportedFunctions.description: Returns a table containing the names of the functions that a resource exports. It will return the exports of the current resource if there is no argument passed in.

getResourceFromName.description: This function is used to retrieve a resource from its name. A resource's name is the same as its folder or file archive name on the server (without the extension).

getResourceState.description: This function returns the state of a given resource

getThisResource.description:
This function retrieves the resource from which the function call was made.

* **Note:**  Every resource has a predefined global variable called ''resource'' that contains the resource pointer for that resource, in other words, the value that this function returns.

getTeamColor.description: This function retrieves the color of a team.

getTeamFriendlyFire.description: This function tells you if friendly fire is turned on for the specified team.

getTeamFromName.description: This function finds a [team](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/team) element using the provided team name.

getTeamName.description: This function gets the team name of a team object.

base64Decode.description:
This function returns the decrypted data from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base64 base64] representation of the encrypted block

{{deprecated|decodeString}}

base64Encode.description:
This function returns the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base64 base64] representation of the encoded block of data

{{deprecated|encodeString}}

debugSleep.description:
[debugSleep](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/debugSleep) freezes the client/server for the specified time. This means that all synchronization, rendering and script execution will stop except HTTP processing invoked by [fetchRemote](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/fetchRemote). This function only works, if development mode is enabled by [setDevelopmentMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setDevelopmentMode) and can be utilised to build a debugger that communicates via HTTP requests with the editor/IDE.

{{Warning|Only use this function if you know what you are doing!|true}}

fromJSON.description: This function parses a [JSON](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/JSON) formatted string into variables. You can use [toJSON](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/toJSON) to encode variables into a JSON string that can be read by this function.

generateKeyPair.description: {{Added feature/item|1.6.0|1.5.9|21055|This function creates a new public key and private key for encrypting data}}

getColorFromString.description: This function will extract Red, Green, Blue and Alpha values from a hex string you provide it. These strings follow the same format as used in HTML, with addition of the Alpha values.

getDevelopmentMode.description: This function is used to get the development mode of the client or whole server. For more information see [setDevelopmentMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setDevelopmentMode)

getDistanceBetweenPoints2D.description:
* **Note:** This function is equivalent to the [Vector2](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vector2) class ''getLength'' method when used with a vector that holds the direction and distance between two points. In other words, it produces exactly the same result as substracting the points' coordinates and getting the length of the result vector.

This function returns the distance between two 2 dimensional points using the pythagorean theorem.

getDistanceBetweenPoints3D.description:
* **Note:** This function is equivalent to the [Vector3](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vector3) class ''getLength'' method when used with a vector that holds the direction and distance between two points. In other words, it produces exactly the same result as substracting the points' coordinates and getting the length of the result vector.

This function returns the distance between two 3 dimensional points using the pythagorean theorem.

getEasingValue.description:
Used for custom Lua based interpolation, returns the easing value (animation time to use in your custom interpolation) given a progress and an [Easing|easing function](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Easing|easing function).

In most cases, either [moveObject](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/moveObject) or [interpolateBetween](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/interpolateBetween) can do the job. getEasingValue is only provided in case you want to do your own custom interpolation based on easing.

getNetworkStats.description: This function returns network status information.

getNetworkUsageData.description: This function returns a [table](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/table) containing network usage information about inbound and outbound packets.

getRealTime.description: This function gets the server or client (if used client sided it returns time as set on client's computer) real time and returns it in a table. If you want to get the in-game time (shown on GTA's clock) use [getTime](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getTime).

getTickCount.description:
This function returns amount of time that your system has been running in milliseconds. By comparing two values of [getTickCount](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getTickCount), you can determine how much time has passed (in milliseconds) between two events. This could be used to determine how efficient your code is, or to time how long a player takes to complete a task.

{{Important Note|The value returned by this function client-side may not be reliable if a client is maliciously modifying their operating system speed.}}

getTimerDetails.description: This function is for getting the details of a running timer.

getTimers.description: This function returns a table of all active timers that the resource that calls it has created. Alternatively, only the timers with a remaining time less than or equal to a certain value can be retrieved.

getUserdataType.description: {{New feature/item|3.0153|1.5.3|9768|This function gets the type of a userdata value, which is not always a [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element) in the element tree.}}

gettok.description: This function splits a string using the given separating character and returns one specified substring.

isTransferBoxVisible.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20788|Determines if the transfer box is visible.}}

setTransferBoxVisible.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20788|Determines whether or not the transfer box should appear to [Player|players](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player|players).}}

interpolateBetween.description:
Interpolates a 3D Vector between a source value and a target value using either linear interpolation or any other [Easing|easing function](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Easing|easing function).

It can also be used to interpolate 2D vectors or scalars by only setting some of the x, y, z values and putting 0 to the others.

isOOPEnabled.description: {{New feature/item|3.0141|1.4.1|6855|This function checks whether ''[OOP](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OOP)'' (Object Oriented Programming) is enabled in the current [resource](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/resource) or not.}}

isTimer.description:
This function checks if a variable is a [timer](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/timer).

* **Note:** This function is not reliable as timer ids are eventually recycled. Always make sure you nil variables containing a timer after it has expired.

killTimer.description: This function allows you to kill/halt existing timers.

resetTimer.description: This function allows you to reset the elapsed time in existing timers to zero. The function does not reset the 'times to execute' count on timers which have a limited amout of repetitions.

setDevelopmentMode.description:
This function is used to set the development mode. Setting development mode allows access to special commands which can assist with script debugging.

*Client-side* development mode commands:

* *[Client_Commands#showcol|showcol](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Client_Commands#showcol|showcol)*: Enables colshapes to be viewed as a wireframe object.

* *[Client_Commands#showsound|showsound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Client_Commands#showsound|showsound)*: Enables world sound ids to be printed in the debug output window.

*Shared* development mode functions:

* *[debugSleep](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/debugSleep)*: Sets the freeze time for the client/server.

* **Note:** Enabling development mode on the server side does *not enable* it on the client side. These functions work independently on both sides

ref.description: This function will create a reference to the given argument.

deref.description: This function will take a reference obtained by the [ref](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/ref) function and returns its Lua element.

sha256.description:
{{Tip|

* The sha module and this function may conflict with eachother, if you use this function uninstall the module!

* This function returns an uppercase string, so make sure you string.upper() anything else you are checking against that has been sha256'd elsewhere.}}

Calculates the sha256 hash of the specified string.

split.description:
This function splits a string into substrings. You specify a character that will act as a separating character; this will determine where to split the sub-strings. For example, it can split the string "Hello World" into two strings containing the two words, by spliting using a space as a separator.

*Note:* You can use the function [gettok](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/gettok) to retrieve a single token from the string at a specific index. This may be faster for one-off lookups, but considerably slower if you are going to check each token in a long string.

tocolor.description:
This function retrieves the hex number of a specified color, useful for the dx functions.

{{New feature/item|3.0156|1.5.5|13977|Added server-side.}}

getProcessMemoryStats.description: {{Added feature/item|1.6.0|1.5.9|21389|This function returns a breakdown of the process memory usage. The reported numbers are always byte units and these numbers can be *inaccurate*.}}

utfChar.description: The function returns the string of the specified UTF code.

utfCode.description: The function returns the UTF codes of the given string.

utfLen.description: The function gets the real length of a string, in characters.

utfSeek.description: The function returns the byte position at specified character position.

utfSub.description: The function returns a sub string, from the specified positions on a character.

utf8.byte.description: Returns the codepoints for the i-th through j-th character of the string passed.

utf8.char.description: Generates a string representing the character codepoints as arguments.

utf8.charpos.description:
Converts the UTF-8 codepoint position to byte-string position.

* **Note:** Code point characters beyond the byte value range (0-127) require at least 2 bytes to represent the character

utf8.escape.description: Escapes a string to a UTF-8 format string. It supports several escape formats, see the formatting table.

utf8.find.description: Finds the first occurrence of the [http://lua-users.org/wiki/PatternsTutorial pattern] in the string passed. If an instance of the pattern is found, a pair of values representing the start and the end of the matched string is returned.

utf8.fold.description:
* **Note:** You may want to read up on [https://www.w3.org/International/wiki/Case_folding case folding] for more information about the use of this function.

Converts a UTF-8 string to folded case (lowercase), which can be used to compare two strings. If ''input'' is an integer, it's treat as a codepoint and a convert codepoint (integer) is returned.

utf8.gmatch.description: This function returns a pattern finding iterator for UTF-8 strings. The iterator will search through the string *input* looking for instances of the pattern you passed. For more information on iterators read the [http://lua-users.org/wiki/ForTutorial ForTutorial] and [http://lua-users.org/wiki/IteratorsTutorial IteratorsTutorial].

utf8.gsub.description:
Returns a copy of the original input string with replaced matches from the pattern by the replacement value.

{{Warning|This function may modify your input string even if no changes were made. Try it with runcode: <pre>srun utf8.gsub(utf8.char(66376), "", "") == utf8.char(66376)</pre>}}

utf8.insert.description: Inserts a substring into input string. If insert-position is given, the substring will be inserted before the character at this index, otherwise the substring will concatenate to input. The insert position may be negative.

utf8.len.description: Returns the length of the string passed.

utf8.match.description: Extract substrings by matching patterns in the input string. This function can be used to extract specific information from a string.

utf8.ncasecmp.description: Compares two strings in lower-case and returns the difference indicator (see table below) as an integer value.

utf8.next.description: This is an iteration function to traverse each single codepoint of a UTF-8 string.

utf8.remove.description: This function removes a substring in a UTF-8 string by using a position range.

utf8.sub.description: Returns a substring of the string passed. The substring starts at ''i''. If the third argument ''j'' is not given, the substring will end at the end of the string. If the third argument is given, the substring ends at and includes ''j''.

utf8.title.description:
* **Note:** You may want to read up on [https://www.w3.org/International/wiki/Case_folding case folding] for more information about the use of this function.

Converts a UTF-8 string to title case (uppercase). If ''input'' is an integer, it is treated as a codepoint and a converted codepoint (integer) is returned.

utf8.width.description: Calculates the width of UTF-8 strings with special/unprintable characters, which require special width treatment.

utf8.widthindex.description: Returns the location, offset and width of the character at the given location in the UTF-8 string.

addVehicleUpgrade.description: This function adds an upgrade to a [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/vehicle), e.g. nitrous, hydraulics.

addVehicleSirens.description: This function adds sirens to a vehicle.

attachTrailerToVehicle.description: This function attaches a trailer type vehicle to a trailer-towing-type vehicle.

blowVehicle.description: This function will blow up a vehicle. This will cause an explosion and will kill the driver and any passengers inside it.

createVehicle.description:
* **Note:** Vehicles (and other elements) created client-side are only seen by the client that created them, aren't synced and players cannot enter them. They are essentially for display only.

* **Note:** Due to how GTA works, creating a lot of vehicles in the same place will cause lag. The more geometries and unique textures has model the bigger the lag is. Even a lot of default vehicles will cause lag if in the same place.

This function creates a vehicle at the specified location.

Its worth nothing that the position of the vehicle is the center point of the vehicle, not its base. As such, you need to ensure that the z value (vertical axis) is some height above the ground. You can find the exact height using the client side function [getElementDistanceFromCentreOfMassToBaseOfModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getElementDistanceFromCentreOfMassToBaseOfModel), or you can estimate it yourself and just spawn the vehicle so it drops to the ground.

detachTrailerFromVehicle.description: This function detaches an already attached trailer from a vehicle.

fixVehicle.description: This function will set a [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/vehicle)'s health to full and fix its damage model. If you wish to only change the vehicle's health, without affecting its damage model, use [setElementHealth](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setElementHealth).

getOriginalHandling.description: This function returns a table of the original vehicle handling. Use [getVehicleHandling](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getVehicleHandling) if you wish to get the current handling of a vehicle, or [getModelHandling](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getModelHandling) for a specific vehicle model.

getTrainDirection.description: Gets the direction in which a train is driving (clockwise or counterclockwise).

getTrainSpeed.description: Gets the speed at which a train is traveling on the rails.

getVehicleColor.description: This function returns the color of the specified vehicle. A vehicle can have up to four colors.

getVehicleCompatibleUpgrades.description: This function returns a table of all the compatible upgrades (or all for a specified slot, optionally) for a specified vehicle.

getVehicleController.description: This function is used to get the player in control of the specified vehicle which includes somebody who is trying to enter the drivers seat.

getVehicleDoorOpenRatio.description: This function tells you how open a door is (the 'open ratio'). Doors include boots/trunks and bonnets on vehicles that have them.

getVehicleDoorState.description: This function returns the current state of the specifed door on the vehicle.

getVehicleEngineState.description: {{New feature/item|3|1.0||This function returns a vehicle's engine state (on or off).}}

getVehicleHandling.description: This function returns a table of the current vehicle handling data.

getVehicleHeadLightColor.description: This function will get the headlight color of a vehicle.

getVehicleLandingGearDown.description: This function is used to check whether a vehicle's landing gear is down or not. Only planes can be used with this function.

getVehicleLightState.description: This function returns the current state of the specified light on the vehicle.

getVehicleMaxPassengers.description:
This function returns the maximum number of passengers that a specified vehicle can hold. Only passenger seats are counted, the driver seat is excluded.

{{Important Note | Only passenger seats are counted, the driver seat is excluded.}}

getVehicleModelFromName.description:
{{server client function}}

This function retrieves the model ID of a vehicle as an [int](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/int)eger value from its name.

getVehicleName.description: This function returns a string containing the name of the vehicle

getVehicleNameFromModel.description: Gets the name of a vehicle by its model ID.

setVehicleNitroActivated.description:
This function activates or deactivates the nitro on the specified [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/vehicle), like if a player pressed the button for activating nitro.

{{Warning|Only works if the vehicle is streamed in.}}

getVehicleOccupant.description: This function gets the player sitting/trying to enter the specified vehicle.

getVehicleOccupants.description: This function gets all peds sitting in the specified vehicle.

getVehicleOverrideLights.description: This function is used to find out the current state of the override-lights setting of a vehicle.

getVehiclePaintjob.description: This function gets the current paintjob on the specified vehicle. <br />

getVehiclePanelState.description: This function returns the current state of a specifed panel on the vehicle. A vehicle can have up to 7 panels.

getVehiclePlateText.description: This function is used to retrieve the text on the number plate of a specified vehicle.

getVehicleSirensOn.description: This function returns whether the sirens are turned on for the specified vehicle.

getVehicleTowedByVehicle.description: This function is used to get the vehicle being towed by another.

getVehicleTowingVehicle.description: This function is used to get the vehicle that is towing another.

getVehicleTurretPosition.description: This function gets the position of a vehicle's turret, if it has one. Vehicles with turrets include firetrucks and tanks.

getVehicleTurnVelocity.description:
{{Deprecated|getElementAngularVelocity|}}

This function is used to retrieve a vehicle's turning velocity for each axis.

getVehicleUpgradeOnSlot.description:
This function returns the current upgrade id on the specified vehicle's 'upgrade slot'

An upgrade slot is a certain type of upgrade (eg: exhaust, spoiler), there are 17 slots (0 to 16).

getVehicleUpgradeSlotName.description: This function returns the name of an upgrade slot name (e.g. roof, spoiler).

getVehicleUpgrades.description: This function returns a table of all the upgrades on a specifed vehicle.

getVehicleVariant.description: This function gets the variant of a specified vehicle. In GTA: San Andreas some vehicles are different; for example the labelling on trucks or the contents of a pick-up truck and the varying types of a motor bike. For the default variant list see: [Vehicle variants](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle variants).

getVehicleWheelStates.description:
This function returns the current states of all the wheels on the vehicle.

No vehicles have more than 4 wheels, if they appear to they will be duplicating other wheels.

isTrainDerailable.description: This function will check if a train or tram is derailable.

isTrainDerailed.description: This function will check if a train or tram is derailed.

isVehicleBlown.description: This function allows you to determine whether a vehicle is blown or still intact.

isVehicleDamageProof.description: This function checks if a vehicle is damage proof (set with [setVehicleDamageProof](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setVehicleDamageProof)).

isVehicleFuelTankExplodable.description: This will tell you if a vehicle's petrol tank is explodable.

isVehicleLocked.description: This will tell you if a vehicle is locked.

isVehicleOnGround.description:
Checks to see if a vehicle has contact with the ground.

* **Note:** This function has a few issues, see below. Consider using the clientside function [isVehicleWheelOnGround](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/isVehicleWheelOnGround) instead.

isVehicleTaxiLightOn.description: This function will get the taxi light state of a taxi (vehicle IDs 420 and 438)

removeVehicleUpgrade.description: This function removes an already existing upgrade from the specified vehicle, eg: nos, hydraulics. Defined in San Andreas\data\maps\veh_mods\veh_mods.ide.

removeVehicleSirens.description: This function removes sirens from a vehicle.

setTrainDerailable.description: This function will set a train or tram as derailable. This is, if it can derail when it goes above the maximum speed.

setTrainDerailed.description: This function will set a train or tram as derailed.

setTrainDirection.description: Sets the direction in which a train or tram drives over the rails (clockwise or counterclockwise).

setTrainSpeed.description: Sets the on-track speed of a train.

setVehicleColor.description:
This function will set the color of a vehicle using either a RGB format, or the [Vehicle Colors|standard San Andreas color IDs.](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle Colors|standard San Andreas color IDs.) Vehicles can have up to 3 colors, most of the vehicles have 2 colors only.

{{New feature|3.0110|1.1|

setVehicleDoorOpenRatio.description: This function sets how much a vehicle's door is open. Doors include the boot/trunk and the bonnet of the vehicle.

setVehicleDoorState.description: This function sets the state of the specified door on a vehicle.

setVehicleDoorsUndamageable.description: This function makes a vehicle's doors undamageable, so they won't fall off when they're hit. Note that the vehicle *has* to be locked using [setVehicleLocked](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setVehicleLocked) for this setting to have any effect.

setVehicleEngineState.description: This function turns a vehicle's engine on or off. Note that the engine will always be turned on when someone enters the driver seat, unless you override that behaviour with scripts.

setVehicleFuelTankExplodable.description: This function changes the 'explodable state' of a vehicle's fuel tank, which toggles the ability to blow the vehicle up by shooting the tank. This function will have no effect on vehicles with tanks that cannot be shot in single player.

setVehicleHandling.description:
This function is used to change the handling data of a vehicle.

{{New feature/item|3.0156|1.5.5|12009|Implemented also for client-sided vehicles.}}

setVehicleHeadLightColor.description: This function will set the headlight color of a vehicle. valid Red Green and Blue arguments range from 0-255

setVehicleLandingGearDown.description: This function is used to set the landing gear state of certain vehicles.

setVehicleLightState.description: This function sets the state of the light on the vehicle.

setVehicleLocked.description:
This function can be used to set the vehicle's doors to be locked or unlocked.  Locking a vehicle restricts access to the vehicle.

{{warning|This function only prevents the player from opening the vehicle doors. It means that a player can still access a locked vehicle if there's an opened door. Also, vehicles that doesn't have doors can still be accessed aswell.}}

setVehicleOverrideLights.description: This function changes the light overriding setting on a vehicle.

setVehiclePaintjob.description:
This function changes the paintjob on the specified vehicle. <br/>

See [Paintjob|paintjob](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Paintjob|paintjob) for list of supported vehicles.

setVehiclePanelState.description: This function allows you to change the state of one of the six panels vehicle's can have. When executed on the server-side resources, the damage will be synched for all players, whereas the change is only client-side if the function is used in a client resource.

setVehiclePlateText.description:
This function can be used to set the numberplate text of a vehicle.

All non ascii characters will be replaced by spaces.

setVehicleSirensOn.description: This function changes the state of the sirens on the specified vehicle.

setVehicleTaxiLightOn.description: This function will set the taxi light on in a taxi (vehicle ID's 420 and 438)

setVehicleTurretPosition.description: This function sets the position of a vehicle's turret, if it has one. This can be used to influence the turret's rotation, so it doesn't follow the camera. Vehicles with turrets include firetrucks and tanks.

setVehicleWheelStates.description:
This function sets the state of wheels on the vehicle.

Internally, no vehicles have more than 4 wheels. If they appear to, they will be duplicating other wheels.

createWater.description:
Creates an area of [water](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/water).

The largest possible size of a water area is 5996&#0215;5996. Also be aware that the function will change all x and y coordinates you specify into even integer numbers if necessary: this is because of a limitation of San Andreas.

You are able to give the water a shallow water effect, which practically changes the water invisible to the eye. However, all elements still work the same way as without the shallow effect - allowing swimming, diving, vehicles to sink, etc.

* **Note:** X and Y positions will be changed to an even integer. i.e. -2, 0, 2, 4 etc.

{{Important Note|If you're working with dimensions, be sure to apply it by using [setElementDimension](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setElementDimension).}}

getWaterColor.description:
This function returns the water color of the GTA world.

*Note:* The server can only return the water color, if it has actually been set by script.

getWaterVertexPosition.description: Gets the world position of a vertex (i.e. corner) of a [water](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/water) area. Each water area is either a triangle or quad (rectangle) so each has 3 or 4 corners.

getWaveHeight.description: This function returns the current wave height.

resetWaterColor.description: This function reset the water color of the GTA world to default.

resetWaterLevel.description: This function resets the water of the GTA world back to its default level. [water|Water elements](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/water|Water elements) are not affected.

setWaterColor.description: This function changes the water color of the GTA world.

setWaterLevel.description:
Sets the height of some or all the water in the game world.

* **Note:** When the water level is 0, the standard GTA rendering is performed so that water is visible when viewed through translucent surfaces, such as vehicle windows. However, some MTA custom objects placed underwater will appear in front of the water. Setting the water level to any non-zero value (i.e. setWaterLevel(0.001) ) forces alternative rendering and MTA custom objects placed underwater will be drawn correctly.

setWaterVertexPosition.description:
Sets the world position of a corner point of a water area.

* **Note:** X and Y positions will be changed to an even integer. i.e. -2, 0, 2, 4 etc.

setWaveHeight.description: This function sets the wave height to the desired value, the default is 0.

areTrafficLightsLocked.description: Gets whether the traffic lights are currently locked or not. If the lights are locked, it means they won't change unless you do [setTrafficLightState](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setTrafficLightState).

getAircraftMaxHeight.description: This function gets the maximum height at which aircraft can fly without their engines turning off.

getCloudsEnabled.description: This function will tell you if clouds are enabled or disabled.

getFarClipDistance.description:
This function will tell you what is the current render distance.

* **Note:** The function will return ''false'' server-side if far clip distance has not been set before the function is called.

* **Note:** Default far clip distance value is 800.

getFogDistance.description:
This function will tell you what is the current fog render distance.

* **Note:** The function will return ''false'' server-side if fog distance has not been set before the function is called.

getGameSpeed.description: This function gets the current game speed value.

getGravity.description: This function returns the current gravity level for the context in which it is called (server or client).

getHeatHaze.description:
This function will return the current heat haze effect settings.

*Note:* The server can only return the heat haze settings if it has actually been set by script.

getInteriorSoundsEnabled.description: This function checks to see if the music played by default in clubs is disabled or not.

getJetpackMaxHeight.description: This function gets the maximum height at which your jetpack can fly without failing to go higher.

getMinuteDuration.description: Tells you how long an ingame minute takes in real-world milliseconds. The default GTA value is 1000.

getOcclusionsEnabled.description:
This function is used to get "occlusions enabled" state.

* **Note:** Occlusions are used by GTA to enhance performance by hiding objects that are (normally) obscured by certain large buildings. However when [removeWorldModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/removeWorldModel) is used they may also have the undesired effect of making parts of the map disappear. Disabling occlusions will fix that.

getRainLevel.description:
This function is used to get the current rain level.

* **Note:** The function will return ''false'' server-side if rain level has not been set before the function is called.

getSunColor.description: This function is used to get the color of the sun.

getSunSize.description:
This function is used to get the size of the sun.

* **Note:** The function will return ''false'' server-side if sun size has not been set before the function is called.

getTime.description: This function is used to get the current time in the game. If you want to get the real server time, use [getRealTime](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getRealTime).

getTrafficLightState.description: Gets the current traffic light state. This state controls the traffic light colors. For instance, state *1* will cause the north and south traffic lights to be amber, and the ones left and east will turn red.

getWeather.description: This function returns the current [Weather](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Weather) ID.

getWindVelocity.description:
This function gets the wind velocity in San Andreas.

* **Note:** The function will return ''false'' server-side if wind velocity has not been set before the function is called.

getSkyGradient.description:
This function will return the current sky color.

*Note:* The server can only return the sky color if it has actually been set by script.

isWorldSpecialPropertyEnabled.description:
{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22195|Added also as a server-side function. Previously only available as a client-side function.}}

Checks if a special world property (cheat) is enabled or not.

getZoneName.description: This function allows you to retrieve the zone name of a certain location.

isGarageOpen.description: This function checks whether or not a specific garage door is open.

resetFarClipDistance.description:
This function resets the far clip distance to its default state.

* **Note:** The function will not reset far clip distance client-side, unless it is relying on a value set by the server.

* **Note:** The function will reset the far clip distance to ''false'' server-side, as there is no default value to begin with.

resetFogDistance.description:
This function resets the fog render distance to its default state.

* **Note:** The function will reset the fog render distance to ''false'' server-side, as there is no default value to begin with.

resetHeatHaze.description: This function restores the default heat haze.

resetRainLevel.description: This function resets the rain level of the current weather to its default.

resetSkyGradient.description: This function allows restoring of a changed sky gradient as a result of [setSkyGradient](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setSkyGradient).

resetSunColor.description: This function is used to reset the color of the sun to its normal color.

resetSunSize.description: This function is used to reset the size of the sun to its normal size.

resetWindVelocity.description: This function resets the wind velocity in San Andreas to its default state.

restoreAllWorldModels.description: This function allows restoring of all world objects, which were removed with [removeWorldModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/removeWorldModel).

restoreWorldModel.description:
This function restoring a removed world object, reversing the effect of [removeWorldModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/removeWorldModel).

You may use [restoreAllWorldModels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/restoreAllWorldModels) to *restore all world models removed with this function*.

setAircraftMaxHeight.description: This function changes the maximum flying height of aircraft.

setCloudsEnabled.description: This function will enable or disable clouds. This is useful for race maps which are placed high up as clouds can cause low FPS.

setFarClipDistance.description: This function is used to set the distance of render. Areas beyond the specified distance will not be rendered.

setFogDistance.description: This function changes the distance at which fog appears. Keep in mind that this function doesn't change the distance of render.

setGameSpeed.description: This function sets the game speed to the given value.

setGarageOpen.description:
This function opens or closes the specified garage door in the world.

* **Note:** setGarageOpen does not work with ID 32 (Pay 'n' Spray near Royal Casino). This garage has been disabled by Rockstar Games due to floor collision issues (see TheJizzy's video "BETA Leftovers and Glitches" at 12:12 timestamp). You can remove the door by using [removeWorldModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/removeWorldModel) and recreating it for later with [moveObject](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/moveObject).

setGravity.description:
This function sets the server's gravity level.

{{Note|

*This will override [setPedGravity](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setPedGravity) applied to peds/players.

*Setting the gravity level to different values on clients can cause animation bugs (players floating across ground because players see different fall animation.)}}

setHeatHaze.description: This function changes the heat haze effect.

setInteriorSoundsEnabled.description: This function disables or enables the ambient sounds played by GTA in most interiors, like restaurants, casinos, clubs, houses, etc.

setMinuteDuration.description: Sets the real-world duration of an ingame minute. The GTA default is 1000.

setOcclusionsEnabled.description: This function is used to enable or disable occlusions. Occlusions are used by GTA to enhance performance by hiding objects that are (normally) obscured by certain large buildings. However when [removeWorldModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/removeWorldModel) is used they may also have the undesired effect of making parts of the map disappear. Disabling occlusions will fix that.

setRainLevel.description: This function sets the rain level to any weather available in GTA. Use [resetRainLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/resetRainLevel) to undo the changes.

setSkyGradient.description: This function changes the sky color to a two-color gradient.

setSunColor.description: This function is used to set the color of the sun.

setSunSize.description: This function is used to set the size of the sun.

setTime.description: This function sets the current GTA time to the given time.

setTrafficLightState.description: Sets the current traffic light state. This state controls the traffic light colors. For instance, state *1* will cause the north and south traffic lights to be amber, and the ones left and east will turn red.

setTrafficLightsLocked.description: Toggles whether you want the traffic lights to be locked. If the lights are locked, it means they won't change unless you do [setTrafficLightState](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setTrafficLightState).

setWeather.description: This function sets the current [weather](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/weather) to the given valid value. To change the weather gradually, see [setWeatherBlended](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setWeatherBlended).

setWeatherBlended.description: This function will change the current [weather](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/weather) to another in a smooth manner, over the period of 1-2 in-game hours (unlike [setWeather](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setWeather), which sets a new weather instantly). To ensure this transition performs as expected, you should not call this function until [getWeather](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getWeather) indicates that no transition is already being done.

setWindVelocity.description: This function changes the wind velocity. The wind shakes the vegetation and makes particles fly in a direction. The intensity and direction of the effect deppends of the wind velocity in each axis.

setJetpackMaxHeight.description: This function changes the maximum flying height of jetpack.

resetWorldProperties.description: {{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22741|This function resets all world properties to default.}}

xmlCopyFile.description:
This function copies all contents of a certain node in a XML document to a new document file, so the copied node becomes the new file's root node.

The new file will not be saved to file system until [xmlSaveFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlSaveFile)() is called

* **Note:** To prevent memory leaks, ensure each call to [xmlCopyFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlCopyFile) has a matching call to [xmlUnloadFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlUnloadFile)

xmlCreateChild.description: This function creates a new child node under an XML node.

xmlDestroyNode.description: This function destroys a XML node from the XML node tree.

xmlFindChild.description: This function returns a named child node of an XML node.

xmlLoadFile.description:
This function provides an alternative way to load XML files to [getResourceConfig](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getResourceConfig).

This function loads an XML file and returns the node by specifying a specific file path, while [getResourceConfig](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getResourceConfig) allows for loading an XML file from a resource.

* **Note:** To prevent memory leaks, ensure each call to [xmlLoadFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlLoadFile) has a matching call to [xmlUnloadFile](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/xmlUnloadFile)

xmlLoadString.description: {{New feature/item|3.0158|1.5.7|19626|This function creates an [Xmlnode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Xmlnode) from a string input.}}

xmlNodeGetAttribute.description: This function is used to return an attribute of a node in a configuration file.

xmlNodeGetAttributes.description: Returns all the attributes of a specific XML node.

xmlNodeGetChildren.description: This function returns all children of a particular XML node, or a particular child node.

xmlNodeGetName.description: Gets the tag name of the specified XML node.

xmlNodeGetParent.description: Returns the parent node of an xml node.

xmlNodeGetValue.description: This function is made to be able to read tag values in XML files (eg. <something>anything</something>).

xmlNodeSetAttribute.description: This function is used to edit an attribute of a node in a configuration file.

xmlNodeSetName.description: Sets the tag name of the specified XML node.

xmlNodeSetValue.description: This function is made to be able to assign values to tags in XML files (eg. <something>anything</something>).

xmlSaveFile.description: This function saves a loaded XML file.

xmlUnloadFile.description: Unloads an XML document from memory.

getRadioChannel.description: The function is used to retrieve the ID of the current radio channel.

getRadioChannelName.description: This function gets the given radio channel name.

getSoundBufferLength.description: {{New feature/item|3.0157|1.5.6|16216|This function gets the buffer playback length of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound). Works only with streams.}}

getSoundEffectParameters.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20914|This function gets the parameters of a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) effect.}}

getSoundEffects.description: Returns the states of all effects of a sound.

getSoundFFTData.description:
This function gets the fast fourier transform data for an audio stream which is a table of floats representing the current audio frame. This allows things like visualisations.

A fast fourier transform generates a table of all the frequencies of the current audio frame which starts at the bass end of the spectrum to mids to highs in that order.

Should you have any problems there is an example resource located on the resources repository:

[https://github.com/multitheftauto/mtasa-resources/tree/master/%5Bgameplay%5D/visualiser Visualiser]

Just type "startmusic mystreamurl" in your console and it will play on the cinema billboard near A51. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundMaxDistance.description: Gets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) max distance at which the sound stops.

getSoundMinDistance.description: Gets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) Minimum distance at which the sound stops getting louder.

getSoundPan.description: This function is used to get the pan level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) element.

getSoundPosition.description:
This function is used to return the current seek position of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) element.

If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundSpeed.description: This function is used to return the playback speed of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).

isSoundLooped.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20785|This function is used to return the current loop state of the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).}}

setRadioChannel.description:
This function sets the heard radio channel, even while not in a vehicle.

* **Note:** This function sometimes doesn't work when setting the radio channel to another different from the current one due to unknown reasons. If you experience this issue, simply add setRadioChannel(0) at the beginning of the script, outside any function.

setSoundEffectParameter.description:
{{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20914|This function sets the parameter of a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) effect.}}

* **Note:** Using this function on a player voice sound element is not supported at this time.

setSoundLooped.description:
{{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20785|This function is used to change the loop state of the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).}}

* **Note:** If the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element) is destroyed by [destroyElement](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/destroyElement) the loop will not happen.

setSoundMaxDistance.description: Sets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) max distance at which the sound stops.

setSoundMinDistance.description: Sets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) Minimum distance at which the sound stops getting louder.

setSoundPan.description: This function is used to change the pan level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) element.

setSoundPanningEnabled.description: This function toggles the panning of a sound (hearing it closer to the left or right side of the speakers due to the camera position). By default a sound has its panning enabled.

setSoundPosition.description:
This function is used to change the seek position of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) element.

Use a player element to control a players voice with this function.

{{Note|

*To set position of a remote audio file, you must pause the sound within an [onClientSoundStream](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/onClientSoundStream) event after creation, set the sound position and then unpause it again. The sound can also not be throttled (see [playSound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/playSound) arguments)}}

setSoundSpeed.description: This function can be used to change the playback speed of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).

setSoundVolume.description:
This function is used to change the volume level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).

Use a player element to control a players voice with this function.

stopSound.description: Stops the sound playback for specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/sound) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element). The sound element is also destroyed.

isBrowserFocused.description: This function checks if a browser is focused.

isBrowserRenderingPaused.description: {{Added feature/item|1.5.9|1.5.8|20806|This function gets the rendering state of a [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/browser) [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/element).}}

isBrowserGPUEnabled.description:
{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|22789|This function checks if the client has the "Enable GPU rendering" setting enabled, which allows the usage of things like WebGL in browsers.}}

*Note*: this is a global setting, not specific to any browser instance and can only be changed by the client.

getCameraClip.description: {{New feature/item|3.0141|1.4.1|6949|This function checks if the camera will "collide" with any objects or vehicles in its way. Read more about this [setCameraClip|here](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setCameraClip|here).}}

getCameraFieldOfView.description:
{{client function}}

{{New feature/item|3.0151|1.5.1|7397|This function returns the field of view of the ''dynamic camera'' as set by [setCameraFieldOfView](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setCameraFieldOfView).}}

getCameraGoggleEffect.description: This function returns what goggle effect is currently affecting the camera.

getCameraDrunkLevel.description: {{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|21795|This function gets the camera drunk level set by [setCameraDrunkLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setCameraDrunkLevel). This function was renamed from [getCameraShakeLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/getCameraShakeLevel).}}

getCameraViewMode.description: This function allows you to get the active camera view modes. This indicates at what distance the camera will follow the player or vehicle.

setCameraClip.description: This function sets if the camera will "collide" with any objects or vehicles in its way. This means that if object clip is enabled an object is in the way of where the camera actually wants to be, the camera will try to be in front of it. This function can disable that.

setCameraGoggleEffect.description: This function allows you to set the camera's current goggle effect. This means you can activate nightvision or infrared effects by script

setCameraDrunkLevel.description:
{{New feature/item|3.0161|1.6.0|21795|This function sets the camera drunk level (as seen on the ''Are you going to San Fierro?'' singleplayer mission). This function was renamed from [setCameraShakeLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setCameraShakeLevel).}}

Drunk effect is a wavy motion of the camera depicting the player being drunk. This function used to be called [setCameraShakeLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/setCameraShakeLevel) which has since been deprecated.

setCameraViewMode.description: This function allows you to set the camera view modes. This indicates at what distance the camera will follow the player or vehicle.

getCursorAlpha.description: This function is used to get the client's cursor alpha (transparency).

getCursorPosition.description: This function gets the current position of the mouse cursor. Note that for performance reasons, the world position returned is always 300 units away. If you want the exact world point (similar to [onClientClick](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/onClientClick)), use [processLineOfSight](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/processLineOfSight) between the camera position and the worldX/Y/Z result of this function. (See example below)

setCursorAlpha.description:
{{client function}}

This function is used to change alpha (transparency) from the client's cursor.

setCursorPosition.description: This function sets the current position of the mouse cursor.

dxConvertPixels.description: This function converts [Texture_pixels|pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels|pixels) from one format to another.

dxCreateFont.description:
* **Note:** The size can't be less than 5 or more than 150. Use this function after onClientResourceStart, otherwise some characters may be displayed incorrectly.

<br/>

This function creates a [DX font](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DX font) element that can be used in [dxDrawText](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/dxDrawText). Successful font creation is not guaranteed, and may fail due to hardware or memory limitations.

To see if creation is likely to fail, use [dxGetStatus](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/dxGetStatus). (When *VideoMemoryFreeForMTA* is zero, failure ''is'' guaranteed.)

=====It is highly recommended that [dxSetTestMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/dxSetTestMode) is used when writing and testing scripts using dxCreateFont.=====

dxCreateScreenSource.description:
This function creates a screen source, which is a special type of [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/texture) that contains the screen as rendered by GTA

Note that successful screen source creation is not guaranteed, and may fail due to hardware or memory limitations. You should always check to see if this function has returned false.

dxCreateShader.description:
This function creates a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/shader) element that can be used in the dxDraw functions. Successful shader creation is not guaranteed unless the [shader|Effect File](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/shader|Effect File) contains a fallback technique which will work on every existing PC.

* **Note:** It is highly recommended that [dxSetTestMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/dxSetTestMode) is used when writing and testing scripts using dxCreateShader.

{{Deprecated items|3.0159|1.5.8|

dxCreateTexture.description:
This function creates a [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/texture) element that can be used in the dxDraw functions.

{{Important Note|This function uses significant process RAM, make sure you don't load a lot of textures, because you'll run out of memory and crash MTA on your gaming PC beyond the technical limit of 3.5 GB (weak PC users much earlier). Besides that, don't make the common mistake of causing a memory leak by not destroying textures (causing dxTextures to pile up) when they should no longer display per your script, which causes FPS lag and crashes all over MTA due to so many scripters missing it}}

* **Note:** The times shown at the right of the page are only the time needed to add the thing to the draw queue, its not the actual time it takes to draw them.

{{Tip|It is recommended to pre-convert textures to whatever format you want to load them as. ARGB should be PNG, all other formats are self explanatory. By doing this you can load textures on the fly without any hickups (Note: There might still be some if the user has a slow HHD). See [https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/releases DirectXTex texconv tool]. }}

[Image:Screenshot_27.png|frame|A speedtest showing the performance of a texture created with various settings of textureFormat.[Mipmaps = true][textureEdge = "wrap"](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Image:Screenshot_27.png|frame|A speedtest showing the performance of a texture created with various settings of textureFormat.[Mipmaps = true][textureEdge = "wrap")]

[Image:DxCreateTexture_mipmaps_false.png |frame|A speedtest showing the performance of a texture created with various settings of textureFormat.[Mipmaps = false][textureEdge = "wrap"](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Image:DxCreateTexture_mipmaps_false.png |frame|A speedtest showing the performance of a texture created with various settings of textureFormat.[Mipmaps = false][textureEdge = "wrap")]

It is possible to use dxCreateTexture to load cubemaps and volume textures, but these will only be useable as inputs for a shader. The Microsoft utility [http://nightly.mtasa.com/files/shaders/DxTex.zip DxTex] can view and change cubemaps and volume textures. DxTex can also convert standard textures into DXT1/3/5 compressed .dds which should reduce file sizes.
